scenario.title: A Future in Healthcare
scenario.subtitle: Ruskin High School · Grade 10
scenario.overview: You are a fictional 10th-grade student attending Ruskin High School. You are interested in healthcare, but unsure how to get started. Your school offers off-campus academy opportunities, and the region has community college healthcare training. Your challenge is to investigate those routes and build a feasible next-step plan before 10th grade ends.

transport_profiles.label: Reliable Transportation
transport_profiles.description: The student has personal or family transportation arrangements they can reliably depend on for off-campus commitments.
transport_profiles.game_effect: Standard requirements apply. Health Start inquiry preparation requires counselor advising and program research.

transport_profiles.label: Transportation Needs Coordination
transport_profiles.description: The student does not have personal transit and must investigate whether district transportation, public transit, or carpooling is feasible for off-campus learning.
transport_profiles.game_effect: Preparing a Health Start inquiry requires an additional 1-action transportation investigation before the plan can be prepared.

actions.title: Speak with a Counselor
actions.description: Meet with your Ruskin guidance counselor to review graduation progress, transcript requirements, and interest in healthcare career clusters.
actions.outcome_message: Counselor consulted. They outline two potential routes: Hickman Mills' Health Start Academy or postsecondary college training at MCC. They emphasize that off-campus programs require planning ahead.

actions.title: Investigate Health Start
actions.description: Research the Health Start Academy details at the Real-World Learning Center: dual-credit options through MCC–Penn Valley, credential paths (CNA, pharmacology tech), and application timelines.
actions.outcome_message: Health Start researched. You confirm the academy serves grades 10–12, awards MCC dual credit, and accepts applications between January and April.

actions.title: Investigate Transportation
actions.description: Check whether Hickman Mills provides busing for off-campus academy schedules and map RideKC bus routes along Hickman Mills Dr and Broadway.
actions.outcome_message: Transportation documented. You verify which class periods have district shuttle coverage and note key transit connections for clinical placements.

actions.title: Prepare Health Start Inquiry
actions.description: Synthesize course prerequisites, counselor recommendations, and logistics into a formal application packet for Health Start Academy.
actions.outcome_message: Health Start inquiry plan completed! You have prepared an actionable inquiry for next school year's cohort.

actions.title: Explore MCC Health Programs
actions.description: Review Metropolitan Community College's Penn Valley Health Science Institute catalog: allied health credentials, nursing certificates, and degree prerequisites.
actions.outcome_message: MCC health programs explored. You learn about the virtual hospital facility, short-term certificates (EMT, phlebotomy, medical assisting), and 2-year RN degree tracks.

actions.title: Compare College Training Options
actions.description: Evaluate trade-offs between rapid entry-level certifications (1-2 semesters) versus 2-year AAS degree pathways (higher tuition and clinical entrance exams, but substantially higher wage floor).
actions.outcome_message: College options compared. You understand how stackable credentials allow earning while learning, building from CNA/phlebotomy up to an RN or radiologic tech degree.

actions.title: Draft Postgraduation Plan
actions.description: Draft a sequenced postsecondary roadmap outlining MCC admission steps, financial aid/A+ Scholarship utilization, and targeted allied health credentials.
actions.outcome_message: Postsecondary inquiry plan drafted! You have an actionable multi-year post-high-school training roadmap.

health_start_prepared.title: Health Start Inquiry Plan Completed
health_start_prepared.description: You built an actionable inquiry plan for Hickman Mills' Health Start Academy. You know the grade eligibility (10-12), the dual-credit partnership with MCC-Penn Valley, the credentials available (CNA, pharmacology tech, phlebotomy), and the recruitment window (Jan–Apr).
health_start_prepared.real_world_takeaway: Health Start offers an authentic head start during high school with tuition covered by the district, but off-campus seat capacity and clinical transit require proactive annual coordination.
unanswered_questions: Confirm exact application deadlines with Ruskin's counseling office.
Check whether personal transportation is required for specific clinical rotation sites.
Verify the dual-credit transferability to your targeted 4-year degree if pursuing an RN or BSN.

postgrad_plan_prepared.title: Postsecondary College Exploration Plan Completed
postgrad_plan_prepared.description: You mapped out a viable postsecondary healthcare pathway through MCC–Penn Valley Health Science Institute. You evaluated stackable certificates (phlebotomy, CNA) versus 2-year AAS degrees (RN, radiology tech).
postgrad_plan_prepared.real_world_takeaway: Community college healthcare pathways provide strong wage ladders in the KC metro, with flexible stepping stones that avoid immediate 4-year university debt.
unanswered_questions: Check selective admission test (TEAS) cutoffs for the nursing and radiology cohorts.
Confirm Missouri A+ Scholarship eligibility and whether high school tutoring hours are complete.
Verify commute times on RideKC Route 47 / Broadway transit lines to Midtown.

still_exploring.title: Exploration in Progress (Partial Plan)
still_exploring.description: You spent your 10th-grade planning time investigating options, but did not complete a finalized pathway inquiry before time expired.
still_exploring.real_world_takeaway: Planning time is a scarce resource. Gathering information without committing to concrete next steps leaves opportunities vulnerable to missed application deadlines.
unanswered_questions: Which pathway would you prioritize if you could run this semester over?
How did your available time and transportation constraints shape what you were able to investigate?
